collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: Two villagers both marked the same fallen hardwood log at dawn: ask the elders, or toss a shell for it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A great log of good hardwood came down in the storm at the edge of the forest: perfect for a canoe. (subject) found it at dawn and cut a mark into it. (friend) found it at dawn too, from the other side, and tied a cord round it. Both marks are there. Both of them claim it.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The elders walk round the log several times. Then they rule: one canoe, built by both of them, used by both in turns. (subject) and (friend) grumble, and agree. It's a very fine canoe. They argue about it every single day, and both of them keep it in perfect condition.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: They agree to toss a shell: white side up for (subject), dark side for (friend). It lands dark side up. (subject) is disappointed and goes off to find another log. (subject.He/she) finds a smaller one. Later, (friend) offers to help carve it, since (friend.he/she) has the tools out anyway. Two canoes are built side by side that season.
